fixtures.label: Multi-destination
fixtures.description: The only MULTI-DESTINATION fixture, and it is hand-built because it has to be: measured 2026-08-23 over ALL 994 prod orders — not the 200-order dev sample this note used to rest on — every single one has exactly one destination, so this shape cannot be captured. Do not "clean it up" into a capture. Two destinations — customer-collecting from our counter (charge window == delivery window) plus a we-deliver stage with a divergent charge window — which is the only thing that exercises per-destination banner rows in the items table, the legend variants, and the conditional Dates Charged row. Items, prices and taxes are drawn from real orders; the organization, contacts and instructions are invented and both addresses are public corporate venues, so it is PII-free by construction and is NOT run through applyPii.

fixtures.label: Flat discount + percent-of-total fee
fixtures.description: Hand-built, and it has to be: it carries the only two money shapes that exist NOWHERE in production. Measured 2026-08-23 across ALL 994 prod orders — not a sample — zero carry a `flat` (dollars-per-unit) DISCOUNT and zero carry a `percent_of_total` transaction FEE. Do not "clean it up" into a capture; there is nothing to capture. Those two arms are its whole job now: the flat-discount arm of the Discount cell, and the percent arm of the totals block's fee row, which prints a rate beside the fee name where the flat arm must not. It is NO LONGER the family's only fee-bearing fixture — `fee-flat-card` (prod order 502, added 2026-08-23) covers the `flat` fee that production actually writes, and all 79 fee-bearing prod orders are flat. Keep both: api-cloudrun#571 switches the Card Fee to `percent_of_total` at CRMS cutover, at which point this fixture stops being hypothetical and becomes the common case, while the flat arm stays live on every historical order. Its percent discount is redundant with five captured fixtures and is not a reason to keep it — the flat discount and the percent fee are. Every money value is computed by @cfs/core/utils/orders rather than typed by hand. Organization, contacts and instructions are invented and the address is a public venue, so it is PII-free by construction.

fixtures.label: Service only, untaxed
fixtures.description: The 6-column floor: the only fixture that drops BOTH the Duration and the Tax column. One untaxed service line, no rental anywhere, no discount — so every conditional column in the items grid is off and the header is just Item Description / Type / Qty / Unit Price / Subtotal / Total. Note it is NOT "the only fixture without tax" — rental-discount-exempt drops Tax too but keeps Duration. Captured from prod order 977.

fixtures.label: Taxed sale, no rentals
fixtures.description: 7 columns — Tax on, Duration and Discount off. A single taxed sale line and no rental anywhere, so this is the only fixture that renders a Tax column with NO Duration column beside it, and the only one whose grid is exactly one conditional wide. Captured from prod order 992.

fixtures.label: Discounted rentals, tax exempt
fixtures.description: 8 columns via Duration + Discount with Tax OFF — the only fixture that lays a Discount column out with no Tax column next to it, because the organization is tax_exempt and totals.taxes is empty. Two of its five rentals are 100% discounted, so subtotal_discounted_cents is 0: the falsy-zero case that made `||` print the pre-discount subtotal. Also carries two sibling groups under one destination. templates#69 listed this order as 9 columns; measured 2026-08-14 it is 8. Captured from prod order 989.

fixtures.label: Taxed rental, no discount
fixtures.description: 8 columns via Duration + Tax with Discount OFF — the commonest real shape: a taxed rental order nobody discounted. templates#69 dropped this order believing mixed-two-tax-rates covered the same combination; measured 2026-08-14 that order carries a 100%-discounted line and renders 9 columns, so without this entry the set had no Duration+Tax 8-column case at all and the two 8-column shapes collapsed to one. Deliberately minimal — one rental in one group — because its job is the column combination, not content. It is no longer the ONLY fixture rendering this combination: `billing-foreign-country` (added 2026-08-23) is also 8-column Duration+Tax, but only incidentally — its job is the foreign billing address block and it was picked for being the smallest carrier of one, not for its grid. This entry is the one that OWNS the column shape, so do not delete it as a duplicate of that one, and do not let a future edit to that one's content quietly become the family's only Duration+Tax coverage. Captured from prod order 991.

fixtures.label: Two tax rates, mixed item types
fixtures.description: The only fixture with TWO tax rates in one order — Chicago Rental Tax 15% on the rentals and Chicago Sales Tax 10.25% on the sales — so it is the only one where the totals block emits more than a single tax row. Note that `taxed-zero-priced-component` also emits two tax rows, but they are a percent and a flat and the flat one is that fixture's whole point; this is the only place two PERCENT rates stack. Also the widest item-type spread in the family: rental, sale, replacement, service and surcharge in one document, with the service and surcharge untaxed beside taxed lines, plus repeated product uids across rows. It renders 9 columns (a 100%-discounted rental turns the Discount column on); rental-discount-taxed, long-multi-group and fee-flat-card share that count and are each kept for a different reason — see their descriptions. Captured from prod order 993.

fixtures.label: 9-column ceiling, single page
fixtures.description: The 9-column ceiling readable in a single view: Duration, Discount and Tax all on, over four rentals in one group with one 20% discount and 15% rental tax. This is the fixture for eyeballing column widths under `table-layout: fixed` — the tightest grid the template can produce, small enough to take in at once. Three other fixtures now render the same nine columns and each answers a DIFFERENT question, so a reader who sees only the column count will delete one of the four as a duplicate: long-multi-group spreads them over ~90 rows across several pages (page breaks, not widths), mixed-two-tax-rates uses them to carry two tax rates and five item types, and fee-flat-card uses them to carry a flat transaction fee. This one is the width reference and nothing else — keep it small. Captured from prod order 943.

fixtures.label: Long order: page breaks + components
fixtures.description: The only fixture under PAGE-BREAK pressure and the only one with real components — two things no other fixture in the family has. ~90 items across 10 groups on one destination, 24 charge days, plus a second long table below it (replacement total $28,847.87), so it is the only fixture that shows group banner rows recurring across pages and whether the items header repeats. It is also the component-indentation fixture: 31 line items are nested under another LINE ITEM rather than under a divider (the Rolling Set Kit carries 16, the pop-up tent 6), which is what the one-em-per-level indent exists to render — every other fixture bottoms out at a group, so the indent is uniformly 0 and the code is unexercised. Brings a third jurisdiction's tax (Rantoul Sales Tax) and `custom-` prefixed line uids alongside repeated product uids. It is the largest file in the repo by a wide margin; that is the cost of the only page-break and component coverage there is, so do not hand-trim it or it stops being a captured document. Captured from prod order 985.

fixtures.label: Replacement only, nothing delivered
fixtures.description: The only fixture whose every line is a `replacement`, and therefore the only one that renders NO #destinations section at all — a replacement charge recovers the cost of an item already lost or damaged in the customer's possession, so we never hand it over and it never comes back: no delivery to an address, no collection over our counter, no date, no address and no contact to print. ⚠️ This supersedes the older note that called it "the only fixture where the dates block stands alone at `--label-col`". That shape existed while the template dropped only the two address blocks and kept the dates; it stated a delivery date for goods that are not delivered, and the whole table now goes instead. `#destinations.dates-only` was deleted from quote.css with it, so this fixture is what proves the section is absent rather than narrowed. Nothing else covers this: orders 978 and 975 are the near misses, and each carries one `sale` line alongside its replacements, which correctly keeps the whole table on. Captured from prod order 976.

fixtures.label: Flat per-unit levy on a zero-priced component
fixtures.description: The only fixture carrying a `flat` (per-unit) TAX, and therefore the only one that renders that arm of the tax cell at all — every tax in every other fixture is `percent` (the one "type": "flat" in `discounts-and-fee` is a *discount*). The flat arm reads the QUANTITY and ignores the subtotal, so it is the one branch that can put real money on a line whose Unit Price and Subtotal are $0.00: 10 cases of water carry a zero-priced `Bottled Water ( /bottle )` child at 24 bottles each, and the Water Bottle Tax bills 240 × $0.05 = $12.00 against a $0.00 subtotal, beside 10.5% Chicago Sales Tax on the $390.00 parent. That is the shape behind templates#107 and manager#306, and it is what the em-dash cell rule and the `hide_zero_priced_components` param are both about. It also pins the non-zero replacement filter from the other side: the child carries `replacement_cents: 0`, so it must owe tax in the items table while being absent from the Replacement Costs table. Captured from prod order 1004. This REPLACED a synthetic fixture on 2026-08-23: the levy was applied to the catalog on 2026-08-20 and is charged on each document's next write, so when the fixture was first written there was nothing to capture and it had to be built by hand from `sale-taxed`. There is now a real one, and this is it. Measured the same day, order 1004 is still the ONLY one of 994 prod orders carrying a flat tax — so if this fixture is ever dropped, do not assume a replacement is available.

fixtures.label: Flat card fee, discounted rentals
fixtures.description: The only fixture whose transaction fee is `flat` — a real $1.15 Card Fee — and therefore the only one that renders the non-percent arm of the fee row. `discounts-and-fee` is the family's other fee-bearing fixture and its fee is `percent_of_total`; the two arms print differently (the percent arm carries a rate beside the name, the flat arm must not), and until this entry the flat arm was rendered by nothing — its colon was fixed blind alongside the tax row's. That gap mattered because flat is what production actually writes: measured 2026-08-23 across all 994 prod orders, 79 carry a transaction fee and every single one is `flat`. There is not one `percent_of_total` fee in the corpus, which is why `discounts-and-fee` has to stay synthetic for that arm and why this one is a capture. api-cloudrun#571 flips the Card Fee to `percent_of_total` at CRMS cutover, after which both arms are live and both fixtures are load-bearing — do not read this as superseding the hand-built one. The fee also sits in its own `Transaction Fees` group as a `transaction_fee` LINE, so it renders twice: once as an items row under its own group banner, once in the totals block. That is the writer's real shape and the hand-built fixture does not reproduce it. Renders 9 columns over two rentals, one of them 60% discounted, under 15% Chicago Rental Tax, on a $41.40 order. Captured from prod order 502.

fixtures.label: Foreign billing address
fixtures.description: The only fixture whose `organization.billing_address.country_name` is not `United States` — a Canadian billing address — and therefore the only one that renders the country line in `#bill-to` at all. Every other fixture bills to a US address, so that conditional was dead in every golden: a green run said nothing about it, which is exactly the failure mode the flat-tax row turned out to have. Not a theoretical shape — measured 2026-08-23, 20 of 994 prod orders carry a foreign billing country: 19 Canada and 1 New Zealand (order 926, which also brings 10 real components if a richer one is ever wanted). Deliberately the SMALLEST carrier available: one rental line ($172.50, 2 x 5G Hotspot over 3 charge days) in one group under 15% Chicago Rental Tax, about 4 KB, so the golden diff shows the address block and almost nothing else. Its 8-column Duration+Tax grid duplicates `rental-taxed`'s combination on purpose — the column shape is not this fixture's job and content was traded away to keep the address the only thing worth looking at; `rental-taxed` still owns that shape. KNOWN ARTIFACT: the postcode renders as `Sample t`, not a masked postcode. `applyPii`'s postcode branch is guarded by `/^\d{5}(-\d{4})?$/` — US ZIP only — so a Canadian `A1A 1A1` falls through every branch to the generic filler, and the comment above that guard already warns this is what happens. Tracked as api-cloudrun#627; when it is fixed, re-capture this fixture, re-bless its golden and delete this paragraph. The country line itself, which is what the fixture is for, renders correctly. Captured from prod order 458.

fixtures.label: Evening boundary (UTC day shift)
fixtures.description: The only fixture whose stored Chicago-offset instant lands on a DIFFERENT calendar day in UTC, and therefore the only one that can catch a date formatted without `{ in: CHICAGO }`. Its `delivery_start` is 2026-04-30T19:00:00.000-05:00 — exactly 00:00:00 UTC — so an unpinned `format` prints Fri 5/1/26 where the order says Thu 4/30/26, crossing a month boundary as well as a day. That is not hypothetical: measured 2026-08-24 across ALL 996 prod orders, 56 carry a `delivery_start` or `collection_start` that renders one day late (58 including the charge window, 121 field renders), because the render container runs UTC — neither the api-cloudrun Dockerfile nor `infra/cloud-run-api.tf` sets `TZ`. Nothing caught it for two reasons this fixture exists to close: no fixture crossed the boundary (the latest time in the set was 18:00 and FROZEN_NOW is midday), so every golden compared the defect to itself and passed; and local preview runs on a Chicago laptop, where the unpinned form is accidentally right. Deliberately the TIGHTEST case available — 19:00 CDT is the exact threshold, so a one-hour regression is enough to fail it. Measured the same day, NO prod order shifts both `delivery_start` and `collection_start`, so one fixture cannot cover both arms; this covers `delivery_start`, the cell that renders on every quote whatever its item types. Three rentals in one group, customer collecting and returning, $402.50, 8-column Duration+Tax grid — content kept minimal on purpose so the golden diff shows the dates and little else. Captured from prod order 872.

fixtures.label: Zero-priced components HIDDEN
fixtures.description: The `hide_zero_priced_components: true` state, and the only fixture in this family that renders it — every other one renders the param's `false` default, so without this the half of the template the param selects is frozen by no golden at all (api-cloudrun#608). Deliberately the SAME source document as `taxed-zero-priced-component` (prod order 1004), so the two goldens differ only by the param and the diff between them IS the param's effect: the zero-priced `Bottled Water ( /bottle )` child hides and its $12.00 flat-tax charge rolls onto the parent, while the totals block still reconciles to $442.95. Order 1004 is the only one of ~997 prod orders carrying a flat tax, so this state cannot be covered by any other document — if the partner fixture is ever re-captured or dropped, this one has to move with it or the pair stops being a controlled comparison.
